home.intro: Nice to meet you, I'm Ágatha! The designer from your neighborhood, your multinational company and your cute indie game. I work with research (UX and UI), illustration and 3D Design.
home.philosophyLead: For me, design is research, illustration and perspective.
home.philosophyBody1: I believe design translates how I see the world and how I'd like to shape it, with an open heart to the people, cultures and stories I come across.
home.philosophyBody2End: as extensions of one purpose: listening to realities that aren't mine and turning them into especially sensitive experiences and worlds.
home.philosophyColUxEnd: brings me closer to other people's lived experience and turns research into a moment of listening and sharing, where we discover things together.
home.philosophyCol3dEnd: , I tell what I've heard in tiny scenes, the kind that make you stop to watch a ladybug climb a leaf.
home.experienceLead: The future lies in human activity, and it is what makes our experiences so important.

pontosSemNo.title: Pontos sem nó
pontosSemNo.subtitle: Brand Identity: Pontos sem nó
pontosSemNo.description: The “Pontos sem nó” brand seeks to transport us to the space between the lines of our deepest unresolved questions that always return to our minds in some way, converting memories into recognizable feelings… (PLACEHOLDER)
pontosSemNo.intro:
The “Pontos sem nó” brand seeks to transport us to the space between the lines of our deepest unresolved questions that always return to our minds in some way, converting memories into recognizable feelings. Pontos sem nó seeks to be part of the moment of identification, conveying the process of acceptance of those feelings in the form of music.

Represented through lines of tenderness, serenity with a lyrical touch that makes us take on the role of a pilgrim in other dimensions through escapism.

creationProcess.title: Creation process
paragraphs: The beginning of the process was marked by guided research, building a semantic board to orient the conceptual decisions of the project. After the research, selections of elements, typefaces, colors and other representations were made to enrich the brand's conceptual repertoire and make its application easier.
images: Visual identity system in six steps: brainstorming of concept words, semantic board analysis, sketch creation, graphic tests, print test and brand identity manual.

images: Final project: brand manual, character library, logo variations and applications.

batucoTuco.title: Batuco-tuco
batucoTuco.subtitle: Batuco-tuco App
batucoTuco.description: Batuco-Tuco is a mobile application focused on the gamification of music theory and instrument practice. Its name alludes to the “batuque” and pays tribute to a Brazilian species and its sound, the tuco-tuco… (PLACEHOLDER)
batucoTuco.intro:
Batuco-tuco was born largely from the opportunity to bring playful contexts into the experience of continuous learning in music. In the Graphical Interface Design course, we were challenged to create an application following a process of requirement prioritization and project management, seeking to understand points of convergence and divergence in order to work on and deliver the application within the scope set in those early stages.

Batuco-Tuco is a mobile application focused on the gamification of music theory and instrument practice. Its name alludes to the "batuque" and pays tribute to a Brazilian species and its sound, the tuco-tuco, inspiring the playful theme and visual style of the project, which turns animals into skilled musicians.

The project was developed as a hands-on study of graphical interfaces and UX/UI. To ensure a smooth evolution with real-time visual feedback, the process involved structuring content maps, building a design system and applying user-centered methodologies.
batucoTuco.heroAlt: Hanni, Yopi, Gunter, Cybele and Pepo playing their instruments together on a lit stage.

lightbox.processAlt: Board of the process stages: 01 User profile, 02 Requirements, 03 Methods, 04 Similar apps and 05 Prototyping, with the little fox's head (Portuguese text).
lightbox.interfaceAlt: Interface board: app screens on nine phones, text about the exercises and the points system and three characters; Assets board with the shop items and their prices in points (Portuguese text).
lightbox.charactersAlt: Characters board: Yopi, drummer squirrel; Pepo, pianist bear; Hanni, violinist fox; Cybele, kalimba bunny; Gunter, bassist cat (Portuguese text).
lightbox.finalAlt: Final presentation: Batuco-tuco logo, the phrase “Your expression matters, and it is knowledge.”, “Music is knowledge.” and two phones with the app (Portuguese text).

creationProcess.title: Creation process
paragraphs: The challenge was to create a scalable design system and cohesive usability flows. To do that, the process was split into five stages, each one feeding the next: the user profile (persona, interview analysis and user stories) showed who would use the app and what they expected from it; the requirements turned those expectations into essential, desirable and performance features; the methods (requirement prioritization, value and confidence attribution matrix, content map and flowcharts) defined the scope and structure of the app; the similar products (benchmarking, rough wireframes and design system) guided the visual decisions; and prototyping gave shape to all of it (next stage).

I prioritized basic requirements, such as the practice activities, to guarantee functionality before moving on to complex band interactions. In the matrices, we realized that playing in real time with other users would hardly be feasible, since synchronization would depend on each person's network.
images: Planning boards: project overview, persona, requirements, user stories, flowchart and prioritization matrix by confidence level.

prototyping.title: Prototyping
paragraphs: From the low-fidelity screens to the high-fidelity prototype in Figma, the main flows of the app are built around theory exercises and a points system. The exercises the user completes earn coins to buy new items for the character that represents them in the game, such as a ribbon bow, a cap, a treble clef and a ladybug.

The characters are Yopi, the drummer squirrel; Pepo, the pianist bear cub; Hanni, the violinist fox; Cybele, the bunny on the kalimba; and Gunter, the bassist kitten. They were heavily inspired by well-known Nintendo and cozy mobile games, such as Animal Crossing and Cats and Soup, with a softer, “cozy” look and approach. In three weeks, I finished the entire interface, the assets and the animations, focusing on optimizing the prototype.

pontinhasSoltas.title: Pontinhas soltas
pontinhasSoltas.subtitle: Pontinhas soltas
pontinhasSoltas.description: Design and 3D modeling of characters around an identity of loose dots. (PLACEHOLDER)
pontinhasSoltas.intro: This work is an extension of the “Pontos sem nó” visual identity manual and brings the “Pontinhas soltas”, the imaginary characters who support the brand, into 3D. More than a project in itself, it was a way to give the little dolls volume and to understand how they would behave off the page, while staying true to the original illustrations.
pontinhasSoltas.heroAlt: Jemmy, Lac, Haggy, Nina and Ali, the Pontinhas soltas in 3D, side by side on a dark blue background with colored lights.

gallery.showcaseAlt: Pontinhas soltas card: on top, Jemmy, Nina, Haggy, Lac and Ali modeled in 3D; below, the same characters in the original illustrations, each with her name and icon.
gallery.flyingAlt: Character illustrations: five Pontinhas flying in a circle and two music boxes with ballerinas.
gallery.turnaroundsAlt: Turnarounds of Ali, Nina and Jemmy: each one from the front, three-quarter and side, facing right (D) and left (E). Labels in Portuguese.
gallery.headsAlt: Character studies: heads and full bodies of Haggy, Ali, Jemmy, Nina and Lac.
gallery.dancingAlt: Sketches of the five Pontinhas dancing in a row.
gallery.cardsAlt: 3D character cards with their concepts (text in Portuguese): Ali is serenity, Jemmy is lyricism, Lac is tenderness, Nina is a pilgrim and Haggy is escapism.

creationProcess.title: Creation process
paragraphs: Each character stands for one of the brand's concepts: tenderness, lyricism, escapism, serenity and pilgrim, and that guided the choice of their shape, color, species and expression. Unlike the low-poly models I usually make for VR experiences, here the dolls were modeled with more subdivisions in Blender, aiming to stay very faithful to the original images. The softer, rounder edges bring that sense of softness and, at the same time, a somewhat plastic texture. They are not rag dolls, but the idea is that their figure comforts whoever sees them, as if they were made of fabric, like plush toys.

prototyping.title: Prototyping
paragraphs: The textures were created in Figma and Illustrator from the identity's own palette (Image 2), keeping the contrasts and the gradient transitions between near-pastel colors that make the characters seem to glow or give off a soft light in the areas where the paint is lighter.
images: Photo of the computer screen with Haggy modeled in Blender and the gradient textures beside her.
Blender capture: Nina's original illustration next to her 3D model.
Photo of the computer screen with Jemmy's model in Blender, still untextured.
Photo of the computer screen with Jemmy textured in Blender and the gradient texture palette.
Blender capture with the five Pontinhas modeled side by side.
Photo of the computer screen with Nina's illustration next to her 3D model in Blender.

finalProject.title: Final project
paragraphs: The final project is made up of the 3D models of the Pontinhas soltas, with their textures, and the 3D printing tests.
